plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is prized in East Asian gardens and is a symbol of perseverance and hope as winter ends.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms often open while snow is still on the ground, and the fruit is used to make umeboshi (pickled plums) and umeshu (plum liqueur).

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It naturally carpets woodlands and meadows and is one of the earliest signs of spring in Europe.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (March to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, Spain and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain the compound galantamine, which is used in medicines for Alzheimer's disease, but all parts of the plant are toxic if eaten.

plants.name: Magnolia x soulangeana
plants.description: A large shrub or small tree with goblet-shaped flowers up to 25 cm across that open on bare branches in early spring. It is a popular ornamental in parks and gardens across temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early spring (March to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated across the southern United States, Europe and East Asia
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants and evolved before bees existed, so they are pollinated mainly by beetles.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up tall, leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped flowers. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere's late summer to early autumn, after the foliage has died back.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand and California
plants.funFact: Its nickname 'naked lady' comes from the way the flower stalks emerge without any leaves, appearing almost overnight after late-summer rain.
